title: Fleet Management
summary: One parking change used to mean an email, 37 folders and a 48-column spreadsheet, edited by hand by whoever knew where the files were. Now it is one app: look up a plate, submit the change, approve it in place, and at 07:00 the fleet list updates itself.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Process design, data model, app, daily automation (with one teammate)

facts.label: Before
facts.value: 1 email · 37 folders · 48-column sheet · edited by hand

facts.label: Stack
facts.value: Feishu Spark · React · NestJS · PostgreSQL · cloud flow to SharePoint · Outlook

sections.heading: Three things in one place
paragraphs: Look up — type a plate, the record and its floor plan come out. Request — the form pre-fills, suggests existing values so one department is not spelled three ways, and takes several changes in one submission. Approve — done in place, grouped by plate, so nothing gets batched and skipped.

sections.heading: At 07:00 the fleet list updates itself
paragraphs: The master sheet still lives in SharePoint, so it still has to change — but not by hand. A cloud flow runs every morning: take the approved changes due today, run two checks, write only if both pass. Either way the coordinator gets an Outlook notice.
sections.quote: It would rather not write than risk a bad write.

sections.heading: Alongside it: a second utilisation figure from GPS
paragraphs: The logbook is filled in by the drivers it measures. GPS gives an independent number — a vehicle is in use whenever it is not at the depot it left from — and the gap between the two is what the utilisation review looks at. Its own page, with the geofence diagrams, comes later.

sections.heading: Next
paragraphs: Search by location, a phone layout, finer permissions.
